assumptions: Illumina's documented color rules for each instrument's SBS chemistry, as cached in the vendor dataset.
limits: Checks color balance only; distance, duplicates and hopping are check_index_pool's questions.
bio.jane/contract.question: Will the sequencer see a signal in every channel at every index cycle for these indexes, on each chemistry?

description: Will the sequencer SEE these indexes? Per-cycle channel occupancy for a set of index sequences under an instrument's own SBS chemistry, checked against Illumina's rules (no dark cycle, both channels preferred, no GG in the first two cycles), each violation citing the vendor article it comes from — and the same set scored across EVERY chemistry generation at once, because XLEAP moved the dual-color base from A to C and a set balanced on a NovaSeq 6000 is not balanced on a NovaSeq X. This is the color question alone; check_index_pool asks it alongside distance, duplicates and hopping for a whole pool.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

barcodes.description: the index sequences to score, one per sample.

instrument.description: the instrument whose chemistry the set is judged under, and whose index-2 orientation applies.

name: check_color_balance

acrossChemistries.description: the SAME set scored under every chemistry generation, so a set that passes here and fails on another instrument says so before the run

channelPlot.description: the fraction of the pool producing signal in each channel at each index cycle; the series are named after the channels, and their colors are not the dyes

cycles.description: per-cycle channel occupancy — the census the tier is computed from

ok.description: whether the set clears every rule for this chemistry

tier.description: Illumina's own grading of this set on this instrument: `ideal`, `acceptable` or `unacceptable`

violations.description: each rule broken, the cycles it was broken at, and the vendor article it comes from
